summary: In Greek mythology, Arsinous (Arsinoos) of Mysia is the father of the Trojan-allied captains Chromis (Chromius) and Ennomus. Homer names the sons in the Catalogue but not their sire; Apollodorus supplies Arsinous. He is distinct from Arsinous of Tenedos, father of Hecamede.

sections.heading: Father of Chromis and Ennomus
paragraphs: Homer's Catalogue sets Chromis and Ennomus — the augur who could not ward off black fate — at the head of the Mysian ships, without naming their father. Apollodorus makes Chromius and Ennomus sons of Arsinous among the allies from Mysia.
Wikipedia's Arsinous article lists this Mysian house beside the Tenedian Arsinous of Iliad 11; the two must not be merged.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id arsinous-mysian is the Apollodoran Mysian father alone. Distinct from arsinous-achaean (Tenedian father of hecamede).
